items.usage: Move to a clearance or approach position at a rapid rate without cutting.
items.notes: Axes move independently at their own rapid rates, so the path may not be a straight line. Verify clearance. The default plane on a Fanuc lathe is XZ (G18).

items.usage: Cut a straight line at the programmed feed rate.
items.notes: The feed value depends on the active feed mode: G98 for feed per minute or G99 for feed per revolution.

items.params: X Z I K or R
items.usage: Cut a clockwise arc in the active turning plane.
items.notes: Arc direction is viewed in the active plane. Use incremental I and K values from the starting point or use an R value for the radius. Full-circle support varies by control.

items.params: X Z I K or R
items.usage: Cut a counterclockwise arc in the active turning plane.
items.notes: G03 is the counterclockwise companion to G02 and follows the same I, K, and R rules.

items.usage: Pause the program for a set time, such as when breaking a chamfer or exiting a thread.
items.notes: P is milliseconds on Fanuc; X is seconds. Check your control's unit.

items.usage: Write offset or parameter data from the program, such as tool-offset or work-offset values.
items.notes: Format is control- and option-specific. Verify before use.

items.usage: Set the normal turning plane for arcs and canned cycles.
items.notes: This is the default plane on a standard two-axis Fanuc lathe.

items.usage: Program coordinates in inches.
items.notes: Sets input units; does not convert existing coordinates.

items.usage: Program coordinates in millimetres.
items.notes: Sets input units; does not convert existing coordinates.

items.params: U W or X Z (intermediate point)
items.usage: Return one or more axes to the machine reference position by passing through the programmed intermediate point.
items.notes: Coordinates on the G28 block create an intermediate move. G28 is not automatically a safe retract, so verify the path.

items.usage: Make a single-pass thread cut that is synchronized with the spindle, similar to a G01 move with spindle synchronization.
items.notes: G32 performs basic threading, while G76 is the usual multiple-pass cycle. The spindle must be in CSS or fixed-RPM mode with synchronization enabled.

items.usage: Cancel active tool-nose radius compensation before a safe exit or tool change.
items.notes: Use a deliberate lead-out that is clear of the part before or while canceling compensation.

items.usage: Offset the tool to the left of the programmed path by the nose radius.
items.notes: This command requires tool-nose-radius and orientation settings on the offset page.

items.usage: Offset the tool to the right of the programmed path by the nose radius.
items.notes: This command requires tool-nose-radius and orientation settings on the offset page.

items.description: Maximum spindle-speed clamp or coordinate setting (control-dependent)
items.usage: Commonly clamps maximum RPM when using constant surface speed (G96).
items.notes: G50 meaning varies by control (some use it for coordinate system setting). Verify the machine manual.

items.usage: Select the stored G54 work offset as the programmed part-zero reference.
items.notes: G54–G59 are the six standard work offsets. Each selects stored values; none measure or set part zero.

items.usage: Select stored G55 work offset.
items.notes: This is the second of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Select stored G56 work offset.
items.notes: This is the third of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Select stored G57 work offset.
items.notes: This is the fourth of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Select stored G58 work offset.
items.notes: This is the fifth of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Select stored G59 work offset.
items.notes: This is the sixth of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Finish a profile previously defined by sequence blocks (after G71/G72/G73).
items.notes: P and Q mark the starting and ending sequence numbers of the profile definition.

items.params: U R P Q W F (format varies)
items.usage: Rough OD/ID turning in repeated passes along a defined profile.
items.notes: One-line and two-line formats differ by control generation. Match your control exactly.

items.params: W R P Q U F (format varies)
items.usage: Rough facing in repeated passes across a defined profile.
items.notes: Parameter letters and cycle format vary by control.

items.params: U W R P Q (format varies)
items.usage: Rough a part by following an existing shape, such as a casting or forging, rather than starting with straight stock.
items.notes: Removes material in a repeating pattern offset from the finished profile.

items.usage: Peck drilling axially from the face; also used for face grooving on some controls.
items.notes: This cycle is especially control-specific. Verify the manual before use.

items.params: R X Z P Q F (format varies)
items.usage: Cut an OD or ID groove with repeated pecks.
items.notes: Cycle meaning and parameter format vary by control.

items.params: P Q R X Z F (format varies)
items.usage: Cuts a thread over multiple controlled passes (the usual threading cycle).
items.notes: One-line and two-line formats differ significantly by control generation. Match your control exactly.

items.usage: Simple straight cutting cycle for OD or ID.
items.notes: On some controls, G90 selects absolute programming. When used as a lathe canned cycle, it performs the cutting cycle. Its meaning is control-dependent.

items.usage: Cut a thread in repeated passes to a defined end point.
items.notes: On some controls, G92 sets the coordinate system. When used as a lathe canned cycle, it performs the threading cycle. Its meaning is control-dependent.

items.usage: Simple facing cycle cutting perpendicular to the spindle axis.
items.notes: On some controls, G94 selects feed per minute. When used as a lathe canned cycle, it performs the facing cycle. Its meaning is control-dependent.

items.usage: Automatically adjust the spindle speed to maintain a constant cutting speed as the diameter changes.
items.notes: Pair with a max-RPM clamp (often G50 S...) so RPM cannot run away at small diameters.

items.usage: Run spindle at a fixed commanded RPM (cancels CSS).
items.notes: Use when a fixed RPM is required by the process.

items.usage: Set the feed mode to inches or millimeters per minute.
items.notes: On Fanuc lathes, G98 selects feed per minute, while G99 selects feed per revolution. Other controls may assign these modes differently, so verify the manual.

items.usage: Set the feed mode to inches or millimeters per spindle revolution.
items.notes: On Fanuc lathes, G99 selects feed per revolution and is the common default feed mode. Verify your control.
